circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Situated on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, the Yas Marina Circuit spans 5. 281 kilometers and was designed by Hermann Tilke to host Formula One racing. The venue has served as the season finale for the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009, establishing itself as a key fixture on the modern Formula One calendar in the Middle East.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting motorsport events. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification for racing.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Styria, the 4. 326 km circuit in Austria originally operated as the Österreichring, hosting the Austrian Grand Prix for 18 consecutive seasons between 1970 and 1987. Following a redesign and renaming to the A1-Ring, the venue returned to the Formula One calendar from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit, situated along Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, is a 6. 003 km street track representing the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. Following its inaugural European Grand Prix in 2016, the circuit established its dedicated Azerbaijan Grand Prix in 2017, becoming a regular fixture on the championship calendar under local operational management.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the first-ever Formula One race in the Middle East that same year and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track accommodates various motorsport events including GP2 Series competitions, drag racing, and endurance racing, while previously hosting Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 to 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design combining extended straightaways with diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driver and vehicle capability. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This 7-kilometre Belgian circuit in Wallonia has been synonymous with Formula One racing since 1950, when it hosted a round of the inaugural world championship season. The venue has maintained nearly continuous Grand Prix status since 1985, missing only two editions in 2003 and 2006, and remains the traditional home of the Belgian Grand Prix.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometer temporary street circuit that serves as the home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its Formula One duties, the venue has attracted various international racing series including sportscar championships and North American open-wheel and stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is a motorsport venue best recognized for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track additionally serves as the home venue for the Shanghai ePrix series beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone village in Northamptonshire, this English racing venue has served as the permanent home of the British Grand Prix since 1987, having first held the event in 1948. The circuit gained historic significance by hosting the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, marking the beginning of Formula One's championship era. Beyond Formula One, the track also features on the MotoGP calendar as a regular fixture.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc in 1986. Built in just eight months following its October 1985 commencement, the permanent track was constructed outside the city near a highway after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's Népliget park were rejected by the government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing facility completed in 1922, making it the third purpose-built circuit globally and Europe's oldest on the mainland. It has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, except for a 1980 closure, earning the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its extended straights and fast-paced corners that challenge drivers.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, featuring a 155,000-person capacity. The track is internationally recognised as a premier Formula One and Super Formula racing destination.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track located in Paradise, Nevada, that navigates through the iconic Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape. The 3. 8-mile course weaves past the city's most famous destinations, including luxury hotels, casinos, and distinctive architectural landmarks such as the MSG Sphere and Bellagio.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 304 km Mexico City circuit honours brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both fatal racing victims whose deaths occurred in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The track has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix during multiple eras, most recently from 2015 onwards under its current "Mexico City Grand Prix" designation, following an earlier stint that concluded in 1992 on a different configuration.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that produces qualifying speeds around 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the track joined the championship calendar in 2022 and has subsequently been adapted for Formula E use from the 2025–26 season onwards.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the urban centre of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, encompassing the harbour area of the principality. It is frequently known as Monte Carlo because the majority of the circuit runs within that particular Monaco neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: The Dutch circuit in the coastal dunes near Amsterdam rejoined Formula One in 2021 to host the revived Dutch Grand Prix, featuring a 4. 259 km layout that has undergone various name changes over the years. The partnership between the track and Formula One concluded after the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Situated north of Doha in Qatar, the Lusail International Circuit spans 5. 419 kilometers with a prominent 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holds an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, a 4. 309 km circuit in São Paulo, opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate racing driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aviation accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise track hosts Formula One racing and features an adjacent kart facility dedicated to Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since its debut in 2021. The track also began accommodating Formula E racing in 2025, establishing itself as a multi-category motorsport destination.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas into its racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straightaways and diverse corner types, making it a versatile test for drivers. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. The track accommodates multiple racing series including MotoGP and the World Endurance Championship, alongside various international and domestic motorsport competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Thai-British driver Alexander Albon races for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 race victories across his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including FIA World Endurance Championship victory, multiple Le Mans 24 Hours wins with Toyota, and a Daytona 24 Hours triumph, making him uniquely the only driver to win both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli began his Formula One career in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, where he has claimed seven race victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team. He has established himself as a competitor in motorsport's premier championship.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabriel Bortoleto is a Brazilian racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Bottas is a Finnish Formula One driver currently racing for Cadillac. The two-time championship runner-up with Mercedes has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his 13 seasons in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One with Alpine, bringing South American representation to the sport's grid.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines a reserve role with Haas in Formula One, where he has appeared in seven races across the 2024-2025 season, while simultaneously competing in the LMP2 category of the European Le Mans Series with Nielsen Racing.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri represents a significant achievement in his racing career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar, a driver holding both French and Algerian nationality, represents France in Formula One racing while driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who holds seven world championship titles, equaling Michael Schumacher's record. He also maintains numerous performance records including the most career race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Hülkenberg, a German racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved success in endurance racing by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 as a Porsche driver.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Racing Bulls.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver for Ferrari, finished as championship runner-up in 2022 and has claimed nine race victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT as a BMW factory driver, while also participating part-time in NASCAR's top series. His Formula One career spanned two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris represents Britain in Formula One, currently racing for McLaren where he claimed the drivers' championship in 2025. Across his eight-season career, the driver has secured 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix victory with Alpine stands as his sole Formula One win to date.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after spending 15 seasons in the sport. He finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while competing for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories during his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver currently racing for McLaren, having secured nine Grand Prix victories during his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured seven Grand Prix victories during his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes in Formula One for Williams and has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 class with Proton Competition, following previous stints in IMSA's LMP2 category.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently competing for Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese motorsport competitor who currently holds a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. Following a full-time stint in the series spanning 2021 to 2025, he transitioned to a backup capacity for 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen competes for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China in motorsport as a reserve driver for Cadillac's Formula One team. The Beijing-born driver competed in the sport's top category for three consecutive seasons beginning in 2022, holding the distinction of being the sole Chinese competitor to have participated in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, when Renault rebranded its works operation to showcase its Alpine sports car division. Following Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the end of 2025, the team transitioned away from being a manufacturer-backed outfit after operating as the French company's official entry for multiple decades.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automobile maker, has appeared in Formula One multiple times throughout its history. The team currently competes under the AMR GP Limited entity as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari HP represents the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari and competes as the sport's oldest and most accomplished team, having participated in every Formula One World Championship since its inception in 1950. The team's iconic emblem, featuring a rearing horse, has become synonymous with the Prancing Horse nickname throughout the sport's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas Formula is an American-licensed F1 team founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014, entering the championship in 2016. Ayao Komatsu assumed the team principal position in 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who led the squad since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering firm, established in 1970, initially made its mark in endurance racing before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. The operation underwent numerous transitions throughout its three-decade tenure in the sport, becoming the fourth-longest-serving constructor by race entries before its 2025 departure. Audi acquired the team and its operations in 2024 to serve as the foundation for its own Formula One venture.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One team headquartered at its technology facility in Woking, Surrey, and operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under the ownership of Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current team based in Brackley and competing under a German licence. The operation became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff from 2022 onwards. Mercedes entries are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows" due to their distinctive livery heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as a second entity within the Red Bull GmbH portfolio alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team represents one of the sport's dual-team ownership structures operated by the Austrian conglomerate.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad represents the energy drink conglomerate's second constructor entry in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by Red Bull GmbH. Founded in 2005 and led by Christian Horner until 2025, the team recently transitioned leadership to Laurent Mekies. Red Bull GmbH also operates Racing Bulls as its second Formula One entry.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and remains one of the sport's established operations.
